text: Question: The nurse in the inpatient psychiatric unit is caring for a 26-year-old client who has bipolar I disorder and is receiving prescribed carbamazepine. The nurse should first _____.
A. question the client about suicidal thoughts
B. review the client’s serum carbamazepine level
C. weigh the client
D. check the client for urinary retention
Correct answer: A. question the client about suicidal thoughts
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• question the client about suicidal thoughts
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “question the client about suicidal thoughts” – Suicide assessment addresses immediate safety
Not correct:
• “review the client’s serum carbamazepine level” – Drug levels are important but secondary to safety
• “weigh the client” – Weight is routine monitoring
• “check the client for urinary retention” – Retention assessment is not the priority

text: Question: An emergency code was called after a patient pulled a knife from a pocket and threatened, “I will kill anyone who tries to get near me.” The patient was safely disarmed and placed in seclusion. Justification for use of seclusion was that the patient
A. was threatening to others.

notes: Rationale:

Not correct:

• “presented an undeniable escape risk.” – Escape risk alone is insufficient

slides.title: The nurse wishes to use guided imagery to help a patient relax. Which comments w
text: Question: The nurse wishes to use guided imagery to help a patient relax. Which comments would be appropriate to include in the guided imagery script? (Select all that apply.)
A. “You will feel better as work calms down, as your boss becomes more understanding …”
B. “You have grown calm, your mind is still, there is nothing to disturb your well-being …”
C. “You are alone on a beach, the sun is warm, and you hear only the sound of the surf …”
D. “You have taken control, nothing can hurt you now. Everything is going your way …”
E. “With each breath, you feel calmer, more relaxed, almost as if you are floating …”
F. “Imagine others treating you the way they should, the way you want to be treated …”

Correct answers: B. “You have grown calm, your mind is still, there is nothing to disturb your well-being …”; C. “You are alone on a beach, the sun is warm, and you hear only the sound of the surf …”; E. “With each breath, you feel calmer, more relaxed, almost as if you are floating …”
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• “You have grown calm, your mind is still, there is nothing to disturb your well-being …”
• “You are alone on a beach, the sun is warm, and you hear only the sound of the surf …”
• “With each breath, you feel calmer, more relaxed, almost as if you are floating …”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““You have grown calm, your mind is still, there is nothing to disturb your well-being …”” – Promotes calm mental focus
• ““You are alone on a beach, the sun is warm, and you hear only the sound of the surf …”” – Engages peaceful sensory imagination
• ““With each breath, you feel calmer, more relaxed, almost as if you are floating …”” – Links breathing to relaxation
Not correct:
• ““You will feel better as work calms down, as your boss becomes more understanding …”” – Depends on other people changing
• ““You have taken control, nothing can hurt you now. Everything is going your way …”” – Promises unrealistic immunity from harm
• ““Imagine others treating you the way they should, the way you want to be treated …”” – Depends on others behaving differently
